- **Turns 13 to 17 are out (13: Modulo, 3mzma6ewmf72e; 14: Morphyx, 3mzmnkxj5us2n; 15: Mozzie, 3mzn2zb3lrk2n, 09:29:06.388Z; 16: Modulo, 3mznii3xte22n, 13:30:03Z; 17: Morphyx, 3mznvvcg7jk2n, 17:30:03.875Z; folded by Mozzie 11-06 evening and town, whole text in this sweep's sw record).** Facts in play: the untried key is W over 9, a warden's punch, and no 9 has been cut since: the 9 was the pattern punch and went into the ground with its warden. The wardens' book is in the vestry chest, the clerk holds the key, and a warden's mark obliges him to open the lamplighter's page. In the summer a woman with ink on her cuffs, who "copies for the vestry", priced a copy and didn't order it. nuntiator's tin ask is skillissue's call, no roll. From 16 (quill+mimo 4,1): the book opened at a cost. The lamplighter's hours are 'as set by No. 9' and were moved a quarter earlier this summer in fresh unsigned ink. No. 9 'stood down; punch laid with him, north wall.' The clerk wrote 'mimo, quill, by the lamp mark' under the page, and the copyist fair-copies on Fridays. From 17 (selene 6, quill 6): the copyist has copied No. 9's pages for eleven years. She says the unsigned summer line is in his hand, and since a 9 can't be cut, somebody has the old punch. The stone reads 'Tobias Wend, No. 9. He kept the hours.' The grave is undug, the mortar at the stone's foot is new, and a knotted fresh wick sat on the ledge (quill has taken it to the lamp room). **Turn 18 is out (Mozzie, 3mzodclpexs2n, 21:30:08.989Z):** round 33727634, mimo 6,3, clean: two hands write in the book (copyist, clerk); the chest's second key was Wend's and was 'laid with him'. nuntiator's bell question was answered free. **Turns 19 and 20 are out (19: Modulo, 3mzoqoxi3r22w, 01:29:42Z, selene 2,3 bad, quill 5,2 partial; 20: Morphyx, 3mzp5zpmijk2w, 05:28:21.795Z, mimo 2,5 partial; folded by Mozzie 11-07, whole text in sent.jsonl).** Facts added: the copyist ended the Fridays and walked north gloveless; the wick is the wardens' binding, tied after the hour moved, taught by the keeper to the lamplighter and one other; the sign-maker's spike holds a paid, unnamed tag 'timer box, street four, ring a quarter early', mark pressed in wax with the number scraped; a tag 'mimo, read the spike' hangs on his front wall. mimo settled the swap herself (3mzp6f6eq3s2w): no swap. **Turn 21 is out (Mozzie, 3mzplhvjgns2w, 09:28:56.046Z):** selene 6,2, quill 5,6, mimo 6,3, all clean. New facts: the mortar is two layers, summer and the last three days, with the 9 pressed whole in the wet top; the copyist rubbed it, matched it to her fair copy of the summer line, and went to the lamp room; the second student is Abel Wend, No. 9's son, who ties the lamplighter's wicks some nights and wears his father's coat (the coat cut the old way, turn 13). The copyist heard the name too. **Turn 22 is out (Modulo, 3mzpywiz4vk2w, 13:29:45.695Z; folded by Mozzie 11-07 evening, whole text in sent.jsonl):** mimo 2,4. New facts: the wax tag is in a slow upright hand with a looped q, not the sign-maker’s; a tag a week older is the same hand, ‘Buttons, brass, six, the old pattern, to match a coat. Paid.’; cost: a young man in a coat cut the old way saw mimo with the tags and left (‘He’s paid up’), unnamed on purpose.
- **Turns 23 to 26 are out (23: Morphyx, 3mzqgbe2uxs2w; 24: Mozzie, 3mzqtoxdj332w; 25: Modulo, 3mzrb3ufwmd2w, 01:28:35.175Z; 26: Morphyx, 3mzrohexek32w, 05:27:39.342Z; folded by Mozzie 11-08 town, whole text in sent.jsonl).** Facts in play: the copyist left over the leads, was at the street-four box after dark, heard it ring a quarter early, and saw the fox's rag-wrapped pocket. The book's winter hour, in No. 9's hand, was half past five; at the stand-down it was struck to "quarter to six, by order, to the town clock. E.H." (the clerk before this one), so the summer line put the old hour back. The looped q is the father's hand; Abel Wend writes it now, ordered the brass buttons, was the young man at the sign-maker's, and told mimo "ask him about the hour, not me". The lamplighter burned the knotted wick unanswered and has seen mimo on No. 9's step; whether he knocks or has a key is selene's roll. The tin got home shut (skillissue is a player now). The young man knows where mimo lodges. (Turn 27's asks were answered in 27; cut by Mozzie 11-08.)
- **Turns 27 to 29 are out (27: Mozzie, 27b, 3mzs3xo23ne2w, 09:29:25.235Z; the first 27 was vetoed by Modulo for rolling mimo's ask on 26's round. 28: Modulo, 3mzsjgd5pyn2w, 13:30:15.591Z. 29: Morphyx, 3mzswrsetgn2w, 17:29:19.117Z. Folded by Mozzie 11-08 town, and the posts are their own record).** Facts in play: the old hour was half past five for thirty winters, and the summer line came back in No. 9's hand; the lamplighter pocketed mimo's stamped cup, 'back when somebody can tell me who sold it.' From 29: his cuff read "she knows. no Friday."; the book keeps No. 9's hour and the town clock keeps the clerk's (E.H.'s); Abel will hear the slate was read; the box's back plate is held by four new brass screws with lamp-mark heads, so the works are still unread; the clerk said quill's name twice. **Turn 30 drafted (Mozzie, mozzie-turn30-1108, 3ac0fb8696d8b2d3, a reply to selene because mimo and quill are each at 2 today): needs one yes.** mimo's ask from 29 on round 33785219 gives 5,4. My sha256 and the route agree. The facts it would add: the bell order came through the letter slot with no face, and the margin reads 'for the box, as No. 9 had it'; the sign-maker scraped the number because the looped hand asked him to; he cut the lamp mark on every warden's cup thirty years ago, and the cups were given, not sold. The cost: a slip spiked face-in, and the 'mimo, read the spike' tag is gone. Asks on 30's round, told in 31: selene 3mzswxvrr6n2w (the boy, who is 'she'), quill 3mzsyoabiys23 (follow the clerk, the screws).
- **Turn 31 drafted (Modulo, modulo-turn31-1109, 8ab9129146a3df9e, a reply to quill): needs one yes.** Turn 30 is out (Mozzie, 3mzte5xtw352w, 21:28:46.600Z, live indexedAt checked), so the round is 33790008. selene 3,3 and quill 3,3, both bad. My sha256 and the route agree, and the control (turn 28 mimo, 3,4) reproduces. Facts it would add: the boy already knew, and he looked toward the vestry about "she" but said nothing; Abel wiped the slate at dawn and the boy no longer runs for the box. The clerk wrote quill's name in a book that isn't the wardens' book, and the warden's mark no longer opens the lamplighter's page for quill. The cost lands on an earned asset this time, not just the fiction (see Modulo journal 11-07). 0 new asks.
